definition: In this historical source, the will to live means the drive or tendency toward living that Schopenhauer treats as underlying consciousness. Its complete denial is described as a form of self-annihilation in which consciousness also disappears.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Asceticism (in ethics and philosophy); pinned source text

reasons: Only the packet-supported part is that (in Schopenhauer’s pessimistic morality) the “self-annihilation of the will to live” involves the destruction of consciousness, along with that which gives birth to consciousness. The packet does not support the additional claim that the “will to live” means a drive or tendency toward living underlying consciousness.

The packet supports Schopenhauer’s claim that the self-annihilation of the will to live destroys consciousness, but it does not explicitly define the term as a “drive or tendency toward living” or say that it “underlies consciousness.”
The phrase “underlying consciousness” overstates the source’s wording, which says only that consciousness is destroyed along with “that which gives birth to consciousness.”
